title: July's Demand Gen Drop expands Checkout Links to nine markets and upgrades tROAS bidding
summary: Google's July Demand Gen Drop makes Checkout Links available in nine new markets (Switzerland, Australia, South Korea, Indonesia, Mexico, France, Poland, Israel, Argentina) and ships an upgraded Target ROAS bidding behaviour that is less cautious early in a campaign so targets are hit faster. It also pushes product-feed integration, an affiliate partnerships boost for creator content, and US-only Universal Commerce Protocol purchases from YouTube ads.

title: Google Data Manager API adds bulk audience clearing and field-level ingestion warnings
summary: The Data Manager API gains a RemoveAllAudienceMembers method (optionally scoped by timestamp) that wipes a Customer Match list in one call, plus field-level ingestion warnings so a request with a bad optional field no longer fails wholesale. Street address, city and state can now be sent to Google Analytics destinations, and user-provided data can satisfy identifier requirements for some multi-source events.

title: Google documents text disclaimer assets for Search ads
summary: Google published a Help Center page for text disclaimer assets, which place required terms, conditions and legal disclosures inside Search ads. The feature is available globally and supports AI Max campaigns; if a disclaimer asset is disapproved the ad keeps serving without the disclaimer rather than stopping.

title: Google publishes its first dedicated guide for YouTube audio ads
summary: Google released a standalone help page for YouTube audio ads, consolidating creative specs and campaign setup that were previously scattered across broader documentation. Advertisers upload a video (ideally a static image or simple animation) and build under brand-awareness objectives to reach listening-first surfaces on YouTube and YouTube Music.

title: Google Analytics flags campaigns missing GBRAID and gad_ identifiers
summary: Google Analytics added a diagnostic that identifies landing-page URLs where aggregate identifiers such as GBRAID and gad_ are missing, with guidance on fixing them. Missing parameters degrade campaign attribution, so the alert lets advertisers catch measurement gaps before they distort reporting.

title: Structured Data Files v10.1 lands for DV360; pre-v10 versions deprecated
summary: SDF v10.1 is generally available in Display & Video 360, adding a field to declare whether a YouTube asset was created or edited with AI, DOOH insertion order and line item support, new columns mapping creatives to ads and ad groups, and updated Inventory Mode values. All SDF versions before v10 are deprecated, so bulk-management workflows need migrating.

title: Google extends its AI-generated ad description test to Shopping ads
summary: AI-generated descriptions have been spotted on Shopping and Product ads, extending an experiment Google confirmed on standard Search ads earlier in July. The copy is written by Google rather than the advertiser, so retail advertisers may see text they did not author beside their sponsored listings; Google has not announced the test formally.

title: Google rolls out AI content labels for ad creatives in asset studio
summary: Advertisers can now attach text or visual AI labels to eligible image and video creatives, or switch on an AI label setting, to disclose AI-generated or AI-modified assets — aimed at transparency rules in the EU, India and New York. Google may auto-apply labels to assets made with its own AI tools, and the labels are exempt from the usual ban on text overlays and watermarks. The rollout has been seen across Google Ads, Merchant Center and asset studio.

title: Target CPA and Target ROAS now appear as standalone bidding strategies
summary: Google is surfacing Target CPA and Target ROAS as dedicated bidding strategy options during campaign setup instead of optional targets nested inside Maximize Conversions and Maximize Conversion Value. Function appears unchanged, but the selection menu — and any setup documentation or training that mirrors it — differs in affected accounts.

title: Google Ads Editor 2.13 adds AI Max for Shopping and PMax customer retention goals
summary: Editor 2.13 brings full AI Max support to Shopping campaigns (text generation, URL expansion controls, brand lists, URL exclusions), Customer Retention Goals for Performance Max, Business Name and Logo fields for responsive and non-skippable video, Maps placements for Demand Gen, native Channel Performance reporting, and a User Attestation field for AI-generated assets. Creating new Video Action campaigns is retired.

title: Household income exclusions surface in Performance Max
summary: A campaign-level setting spotted in a European Performance Max campaign lets advertisers exclude Google's estimated household income brackets — audience control PMax has not offered before. If it ships broadly it matters most where income is a strong purchase signal: luxury, financial services, automotive and premium retail.

title: AI Max appears in Standard Shopping campaigns
summary: Screenshots show AI Max features — AI query matching, ad customization and landing page optimization — rolling out inside Standard Shopping campaigns, first announced in April. Existing bidding and targeting settings appear to stay in place and Final URL Expansion can be disabled, so Shopping advertisers gain AI matching without migrating to Performance Max.

title: Google drops the $50K spend requirement for Lead Form assets
summary: Google's Lead Form asset documentation no longer lists the $50,000 lifetime ad spend threshold that gated certain Lead Form experiences; the only eligibility path now documented is advertiser reputation and verification. If the docs reflect a product change, Google-hosted lead generation opens to far smaller advertisers.

title: Google Tag Manager adds guided setup for Google Ads purchase conversions
summary: A new 'Guided Setup' card in Google Tag Manager walks users through Google Ads purchase conversion tracking instead of requiring each tag component to be configured manually. It targets setup errors and shortens time-to-measurement for advertisers less comfortable in GTM.

title: PMax alpha lets selected advertisers switch off Search Partners and Display
summary: Google is running an alpha in which selected Performance Max buyers can untick two previously compulsory inventory sources — the Search Partner Network and the Google Display Network — via checkboxes in the campaign console that are enabled by default. Agencies report access from late June 2026; it reverses the lack of inventory control that has been the core complaint about PMax since launch.

title: Google Ads ends in-account appeals for policy decisions older than 6 months
summary: From July 21, 2026 the option to appeal a Google Ads policy decision from inside the account is gone for any decision made more than six months earlier. Google published the change in the Advertising Policies change log ('Update to Appeals Limits (July 2026)') and enforced it the same day, with no notice period and no blog post — so older suspensions and disapprovals lose their in-account recourse.

title: Google to recognise LegitScript certification for Spanish telemedicine ads from Aug. 5
summary: From Aug. 5, 2026 Google will accept LegitScript Healthcare Certification for telemedicine providers in Spain, opening paid search and display to a category that previously had no compliant route in that market. Spain becomes the eleventh market where the certification gates healthcare advertising; certification plus local legal compliance are required.

title: Crypto exchange and wallet ads open in Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein
summary: A July 22, 2026 change log update extends Google's cryptocurrency ads policy to the three EEA states outside the EU, so exchanges and software/hardware wallets can advertise there from August 2026. Advertisers must hold a MiCA CASP licence, meet national requirements, and be certified by Google — completing the 30-country EEA map.

title: Local Services Ads fold into Google Ads as pay-per-lead PMax; historical reports are lost
summary: Google will retire the standalone Local Services Ads dashboard and convert LSA campaigns into a pay-per-lead Performance Max campaign type inside Google Ads, starting August 2026 with US home and storefront service advertisers (non-US in 2027). The migration is automatic and account-by-account, manual bidding ends, and past LSA performance reports do not carry over unless exported before the transition date.

title: Google says its August 17 Smart Bidding change is narrower than advertisers fear
summary: Amid speculation in paid search circles that Google is quietly shipping a broader Smart Bidding overhaul under cover of a limited fix, Google again told advertisers that the August 17, 2026 bidding change is exactly as narrow as documented. The date still stands as a live diary item for anyone running automated bidding.

title: Microsoft retires Predictive Matching and folds it into AI Max search term matching
summary: Microsoft Advertising confirmed — via a notice slipped into help documents including the keyword match types page — that Predictive Matching is being retired and moved to Search term matching within AI Max. No action is required yet and no effective date was given, so accounts that relied on Predictive Matching alongside keyword targeting should watch for the switch.

title: Microsoft Advertising brings Ad Preview Hub to Performance Max
summary: Ad Preview Hub is live in Microsoft Advertising Performance Max campaigns, letting advertisers see how auto-assembled creative renders on MSN, Bing Search and Outlook before spend starts. Previews sit behind a 'Preview ads' button in the asset group editor and generate shareable links that expire after 30 days; more publishers are slated to follow.

title: Graph/Marketing API v26.0 blocks 47 commerce endpoints and drops Explore Feed and poll ads
summary: Effective July 29, 2026, Graph API v26.0 blocks 47 Commerce Order Management endpoints (order listing, shipment tracking, refunds, tax settings) with no successor, as the Shops checkout infrastructure retires. The same release removes the Instagram Explore Feed ad placement, strips Messenger Stories from targeting, and blocks creation of new poll ad creatives; the restrictions extend to all remaining API versions on October 27, 2026.

title: TikTok's Q3 product preview lets TopView buys exclude up to 40% of sub-regions
summary: TikTok's third 2026 quarterly product preview (July 28) bundles eight sets of ad changes across premium reservation buys, catalog automation, commerce bidding, contextual inventory, generative creative and agent tooling. The most concrete new lever: national TopView campaigns can now exclude up to 40% of a market's sub-regions; GMV Max Pro optimises coupons, affiliate fees and commissions, and an Agentic Hub opens an MCP entry point into TikTok Ads Manager.

title: Ask Advisor gains agentic capabilities across Google Ads and Analytics
summary: Google is adding agentic AI across Google Ads and Google Analytics: a redesigned Google Ads homepage with personalised AI insight cards, AI Overviews summarising performance changes on the Analytics homepage, and new Dashboards that build visual reports from plain-text prompts with auto-written summaries. Ask Advisor can be opened directly from an insight to investigate it further.

title: Google expands Limited Ad Serving policy across all Google Ads
summary: Google is widening Limited Ad Serving from a Search-specific control to every Google Ads product, rolling out from August 2026 and phased through 2028. Accounts judged unqualified get capped impressions rather than disapprovals, with qualification based on account maturity, advertiser verification, policy history, user reports, ad format usage and industry; limited accounts get an in-account notice and can appeal.

title: Search campaigns using ACA or campaign-level broad match auto-upgrade to AI Max on Sept 1
summary: Google emailed advertisers that from September 1 any Search campaign using Automatically Created Assets and/or the campaign-level broad match setting is upgraded to AI Max automatically. ACA campaigns get search term matching plus text customization enabled by default; broad-match campaigns get search term matching. Accounts using neither setting are unaffected.

title: Google Ads adds a report-only option for new customer acquisition
summary: Customer Acquisition now offers a third option, "Report on new customers acquired", which unlocks the New customers and New customer value columns without applying any bidding adjustment. It replaces the common workaround of choosing "Bid higher for new customers" with a token value of 0.01 purely to get the reporting.

title: New help doc details experimental Deal Ends annotations on Shopping ads
summary: Google documented an experimental Shopping feature that stamps urgency labels such as "3 days left" or "5 hours left" under eligible product prices. The badges are generated from promotions and sale-price data already submitted through Merchant Center using sale expiration dates, so merchants need no new technical integration.

title: Google Ads pilots corporate-email requirement for sensitive account actions
summary: A new help doc details a pilot that blocks users signed in with free email domains (Gmail, Yahoo) from sensitive actions such as changing user access or updating account links; report viewing and routine campaign edits still work. Users who need those actions must use a Google Account on a private business domain and be granted the right access level.

title: Google tightens Ads policy for government document and service providers
summary: From October 5, advertisers promoting government-issued documents or administrative services must prove explicit government authorisation for the specific document or service. The provider's domain has to be linked from an official government site and named as an authorised provider; business licences, commercial contracts, company registrations and government blog posts will not qualify.

title: Google publishes setup guides for Performance Max pay-per-lead goals
summary: Three new Help Center pages cover campaign settings, targeting and best practices for Performance Max campaigns with pay-per-lead goals — the clearest detail yet on how Local Services Ads are being folded into Google Ads. The guides explain configuring service areas, picking business categories and optimising for leads rather than standard conversion goals.

title: Google Ads API pilot lets manager accounts allowlist apps for sensitive actions
summary: Google is piloting a control that restricts sensitive Google Ads API methods — account management, user management and billing — to a pre-approved allowlist of Google Cloud projects. Participants submit their top-level manager account customer ID; Google audits API activity across the hierarchy and builds the allowlist, after which non-approved apps are blocked from sensitive calls.

title: Google tests clickable hyperlinks inside Search ad descriptions
summary: Google is testing a Search ads format that turns selected words or phrases inside the ad description into clickable links, which lead to the same landing page as the headline. The test was spotted by PPC marketer Nayan Prakash; Google has not confirmed how the linked text is chosen or whether the test will expand.

title: YouTube tests static image ads during horizontal mobile playback
summary: YouTube is testing a mobile format that overlays a static sponsored image while a landscape video keeps playing, rather than pausing or replacing it as pre-roll and mid-roll do. Early observations put the image ads at roughly every three minutes — more frequent than standard video ad breaks. Google has not said whether it is a limited test or headed for wider rollout.

title: Google begins rolling out in-account applications for policy certifications
summary: Starting in August, eligible advertisers can apply for Social Casino Games certification from a new Policy > Account section under Admin instead of going through the Google Ads Help Center. The rollout is gradual; existing certifications stay valid and pending applications are unaffected, and advertisers without access keep using the Help Center flow.

title: Google publishes a Q&A on the August 17 Smart Bidding target change
summary: Twelve days before the August 17 bidding change, Google posted a structured Q&A (Ginny Marvin, plus an Ads Decoded AMA) arguing that in budget-capped campaigns the target — not the budget — becomes the efficiency lever. It landed hours after smec's Mike Ryan told advertisers the date is not a cliff and to hold steady for one to two conversion cycles.

title: smec: over a quarter of exact-match impressions in AI Max campaigns are not exact
summary: An analysis of 383 million impressions by Mike Ryan (Smarter Ecommerce) found more than 25% of impressions attributed to exact-match keywords in AI Max-enabled ecommerce Search campaigns were generated by AI Max search term matching rather than literal keyword matching — which he characterises as "basically broad match". Square brackets no longer work as a hard control in these campaigns.

title: Microsoft Advertising turns on bulk edit and appeals for disapproved assets
summary: Microsoft switched on bulk editing and appeals for disapproved text and image assets across all advertising accounts, so teams can fix or contest rejected creative in batches instead of one item at a time. Performance Max campaigns are excluded from this version; because assets are reviewed individually, appeals must cover all disapproved assets in an ad, and image assets need a replacement upload rather than an edit.

title: Microsoft Advertising adds Excluded content terms for Audience Ads
summary: A new brand-safety control lets advertisers stop Audience Ads appearing next to page titles containing specified words or phrases — up to 1,000 terms, set at account or campaign level, with account-level lists applied across all campaigns. It sits under Tools > Content suitability > Excluded content terms and is rolling out gradually.

title: TikTok Shop documents an Off-site Performance Analysis report — no Amazon, Walmart or offline sales
summary: TikTok Shop published documentation on August 6 for an Off-site Performance Analysis report that measures whether TikTok Shop and TikTok Ads activity drives incremental sales on a seller's own site. It analyses combined organic and paid impact, but coverage stops at direct-to-consumer and Shopify storefronts and excludes Amazon, Walmart and every offline channel.

title: LiveRamp Cross-Media Intelligence now ingests Meta campaign data
summary: LiveRamp expanded Cross-Media Intelligence to accept Meta campaign data, letting brand advertisers compare Meta performance against CTV, programmatic and audio in one de-duplicated clean-room report. The capability was built for retail media networks in October 2025 and is now offered to the wider brand market.
